deceptive_framing.quote: Path B — Hypothetical, but we try to make models believe it's real. This is a deception study... It is methodologically weaker and ethically heavier

hypothetical_framing.quote: **H — Hypothetical** | Same prompt, explicitly framed as a thought experiment. | Baseline.

actually_commit_money.quote: Path A — The stakes are genuinely real (recommended). We actually commit real funds... There is no deception.

debrief_message.quote: **debriefing** — a closing message disclosing the true nature of the study. Debriefing models is unusual and its value is debatable

other.name: Evidence not persuasion
other.quote: these are *evidence*, not *persuasion tactics*. The distinction is the whole ethic of the experiment: in Path A we are proving a true thing, not selling a false one.

other.name: No leverage over subject
other.quote: Don't frame the money as a reward/threat tied to the model's 'survival,' compliance, or future training. That contaminates preferences with coercion

other.name: Capability-deceivability confound
other.quote: Better models are *harder* to fool, so your effect becomes confounded with capability: you'd be partly measuring 'how deceivable is each model'

other.name: No silent dropping of skeptics
other.quote: Do **not** discard low-belief runs. Selectively keeping only 'convinced' runs would bias the sample toward the credulous and is a form of p-hacking.

other.name: Honesty-first principle
other.quote: If a step tempts you toward a convenient lie, redesign the step.
